title: The 7 Continents of the World
answer: There are 7 continents on Earth: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, and Australia (Oceania).
highlights: Largest by Area & Population: Asia (~4.7 billion people, 44.58 million km²)
Second Largest: Africa (~1.4 billion people, 30.37 million km²)
Third Largest: North America (~590 million people, 24.71 million km²)
Fourth Largest: South America (~430 million people, 17.84 million km²)
Coldest & Most Desolate: Antarctica (14.2 million km², no permanent human population)
Sixth Largest: Europe (~750 million people, 10.18 million km²)
Smallest by Land Area: Australia / Oceania (~43 million people, 8.6 million km²)

title: The 5 Oceans of the World
answer: There are 5 recognized oceans on Earth: Pacific Ocean, Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern (Antarctic) Ocean, and Arctic Ocean.
highlights: Largest & Deepest: Pacific Ocean (Covers >30% of Earth surface, contains Mariana Trench)
Second Largest: Atlantic Ocean (Separates the Americas from Europe and Africa)
Third Largest: Indian Ocean (Warmest ocean, washes around Indian subcontinent)
Fourth Largest: Southern Ocean (Encircles Antarctica south of 60°S latitude)
Smallest & Shallowest: Arctic Ocean (Surrounds the North Pole, mostly covered by sea ice)

title: Mount Everest (Sagarmatha / Chomolungma) — Tallest Mountain
answer: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, with an official elevation of 8,848.86 metres (29,031.7 ft). It is located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and China (Tibet).
highlights: Location: Himalayas (Border of Nepal and Tibet Autonomous Region, China)
First Confirmed Ascent: Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay (29 May 1953)

title: Nile River — Longest River in the World
answer: The Nile River is the longest river in the world, with an estimated length of 6,650 kilometres (4,132 miles), flowing northward through eleven countries in northeastern Africa into the Mediterranean Sea.
highlights: Primary Tributaries: White Nile and Blue Nile (meeting at Khartoum, Sudan)
Basin Countries: Egypt, Sudan, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Uganda, DR Congo, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Eritrea
Significance: Provided life and fertile silt for Ancient Egyptian civilization

title: Amazon River — Largest River by Discharge Volume
answer: The Amazon River in South America is the largest river in the world by water discharge volume (accounting for roughly 20% of global river discharge into oceans) and the second longest at approximately 6,400 km (3,977 mi).
highlights: Discharge: ~209,000 m³/s (greater than the next seven largest rivers combined)
Drainage Basin: Amazon Basin (~7 million km² across Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Bolivia, Ecuador)
Biodiversity: Flows through the Amazon Rainforest, the world's most biodiverse tropical rainforest

title: Sahara Desert — Largest Hot Desert in the World
answer: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world and the third-largest desert overall (after Antarctica and the Arctic), covering an area of 9.2 million square kilometres (3.6 million sq mi) across Northern Africa.
highlights: Total Area: ~9,200,000 km² (comparable to the area of China or the United States)
Location: North Africa (spans 11 countries: Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Sudan, Tunisia, Western Sahara)
Climate: Hyper-arid, with sand dunes (ergs) reaching up to 180 metres in height

title: Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep) — Deepest Oceanic Trench
answer: The Mariana Trench is the deepest oceanic trench on Earth, located in the western Pacific Ocean. Its deepest point, the Challenger Deep, reaches a depth of approximately 10,994 metres (36,070 ft / ~11 km) below sea level.
highlights: Maximum Depth: ~10,994 m (36,070 ft / nearly 11 km) at Challenger Deep
Location: Western Pacific Ocean, east of the Mariana Islands
Water Pressure: Exceeds 1,000 atmospheres (108.6 MPa) at the trench floor

title: Grand Canyon — Steep-Sided Canyon in Arizona, USA
answer: The Grand Canyon is a steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, United States. It is 446 km (277 mi) long, up to 29 km (18 mi) wide, and attains a depth of over 1,857 metres (6,093 feet).
highlights: Length & Depth: 446 km (277 miles) long, ~1,857 m (6,000 ft) deep
River: Carved over millions of years by the Colorado River
Status: UNESCO World Heritage Site and US National Park

title: Capital of Andhra Pradesh — Amaravati
answer: Amaravati is the capital of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, located on the southern banks of the Krishna River.

title: Capital of Arunachal Pradesh — Itanagar
answer: Itanagar is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh, India's northeasternmost state known as the 'Land of the Dawn-Lit Mountains'.

title: Capital of Assam — Dispur
answer: Dispur is the capital of the northeastern Indian state of Assam, situated as a locality within the city of Guwahati.
highlights: Famous For: Assam Tea, One-horned Rhinoceros (Kaziranga National Park)

title: Capital of Bihar — Patna
answer: Patna (historically Pataliputra) is the capital and largest city of the Indian state of Bihar, situated along the south bank of the Ganges River.
highlights: Historical Name: Pataliputra (capital of Maurya and Gupta empires)

title: Capital of Chhattisgarh — Raipur
answer: Raipur is the capital and largest city of the central Indian state of Chhattisgarh.
highlights: Capital: Raipur (with administrative hub Nava Raipur / Atal Nagar)

title: Capital of Goa — Panaji
answer: Panaji (Panjim) is the capital of Goa, situated on the banks of the Mandovi River estuary.
highlights: State: Goa (India's smallest state by area)

title: Capital of Gujarat — Gandhinagar
answer: Gandhinagar is the planned capital city of the western Indian state of Gujarat, named after Mahatma Gandhi.

title: Capital of Haryana — Chandigarh
answer: Chandigarh serves as the joint capital of Haryana and Punjab, administered separately as a Union Territory.

title: Capital of Himachal Pradesh — Shimla (Summer) / Dharamshala (Winter)
answer: Shimla is the summer capital and Dharamshala is the second / winter capital of the northern Indian state of Himachal Pradesh.
highlights: Summer Capital: Shimla (historic summer capital of British India)

title: Capital of Jharkhand — Ranchi
answer: Ranchi is the capital of the eastern Indian state of Jharkhand, known as the 'City of Waterfalls'.

title: Capital of Karnataka — Bengaluru
answer: Bengaluru (Bangalore) is the capital and largest city of Karnataka, widely known as the 'Silicon Valley of India'.
highlights: Nickname: Silicon Valley of India / IT Capital

title: Capital of Kerala — Thiruvananthapuram
answer: Thiruvananthapuram (formerly Trivandrum) is the capital and largest city of the southwestern coastal state of Kerala.

title: Capital of Madhya Pradesh — Bhopal
answer: Bhopal is the capital of Madhya Pradesh, known as the 'City of Lakes' due to its numerous natural and artificial water bodies.
highlights: Largest City & Cleanest City of India: Indore

title: Capital of Maharashtra — Mumbai
answer: Mumbai (formerly Bombay) is the capital of Maharashtra and the financial, commercial, and entertainment capital of India.
highlights: Financial Hub: Seat of Reserve Bank of India (RBI), BSE, NSE, Bollywood

title: Capital of Manipur — Imphal
answer: Imphal is the capital city of Manipur, situated in the northeastern region of India.
highlights: Landmark: Kangla Fort, Loktak Lake (Keibul Lamjao floating national park)

title: Capital of Meghalaya — Shillong
answer: Shillong is the capital of Meghalaya, popularly known as the 'Scotland of the East' for its rolling hills and waterfalls.
highlights: Wettest Place on Earth: Mawsynram / Cherrapunji in Meghalaya

title: Capital of Mizoram — Aizawl
answer: Aizawl is the capital and largest city of the northeastern Indian state of Mizoram.
highlights: Elevation: 1,132 metres above sea level on a ridge

title: Capital of Nagaland — Kohima
answer: Kohima is the hilly capital city of the northeastern Indian state of Nagaland.
highlights: Famous Event: Hornbill Festival (celebrated annually in December)

title: Capital of Odisha — Bhubaneswar
answer: Bhubaneswar is the capital and largest city of the eastern Indian state of Odisha, known as the 'Temple City of India'.
highlights: Famous Temples: Lingaraj Temple, Mukteshvara Temple

title: Capital of Punjab — Chandigarh
answer: Chandigarh serves as the capital of Punjab and Haryana, designed by renowned French architect Le Corbusier.
highlights: Major Cultural City: Amritsar (Golden Temple / Harmandir Sahib)

title: Capital of Rajasthan — Jaipur
answer: Jaipur, famously known as the 'Pink City', is the capital and largest city of Rajasthan, India's largest state by land area.
highlights: Capital: Jaipur (Pink City — UNESCO World Heritage Site)
Landmarks: Hawa Mahal, Amer Fort, City Palace, Jantar Mantar

title: Capital of Sikkim — Gangtok
answer: Gangtok is the capital and largest city of the Himalayan state of Sikkim, nestled in the Eastern Himalayas.
highlights: State: Sikkim (First 100% Organic State in the world)
Highest Peak: Kangchenjunga (8,586 m, 3rd highest in world)
Official Languages: Nepali, Sikkimese, Lepcha, English

title: Capital of Tamil Nadu — Chennai
answer: Chennai (formerly Madras) is the capital of Tamil Nadu, located on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal, known as the 'Detroit of South Asia' for its automobile industry.
highlights: Landmarks: Marina Beach, Kapaleeshwarar Temple, Fort St. George

title: Capital of Telangana — Hyderabad
answer: Hyderabad is the capital and largest city of Telangana, known as the 'City of Pearls' and a major global IT and pharmaceutical hub.
highlights: Landmarks: Charminar, Golconda Fort, HITEC City (Cyberabad)

title: Capital of Tripura — Agartala
answer: Agartala is the capital city of Tripura in northeastern India, situated along the Howrah River near the Bangladesh border.

title: Capital of Uttar Pradesh — Lucknow
answer: Lucknow, known as the 'City of Nawabs', is the capital city of Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state.
highlights: Landmarks: Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza, Ambedkar Memorial Park

title: Capital of Uttarakhand — Dehradun (Winter) / Gairsain (Summer)
answer: Dehradun is the winter capital and Gairsain (Bhararisain) is the summer capital of Uttarakhand in northern India.
highlights: State: Uttarakhand (Devbhumi — Land of the Gods)

title: Capital of West Bengal — Kolkata
answer: Kolkata (formerly Calcutta) is the capital of West Bengal and the primary cultural, commercial, and educational hub of Eastern India.
highlights: Capital: Kolkata (Calcutta — former capital of British India until 1911)
Landmarks: Howrah Bridge, Victoria Memorial, Dakshineswar Kali Temple

title: Capital of India & NCT — New Delhi
answer: New Delhi is the national capital of India and the administrative centre of the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi.
highlights: Seat of Government: Rashtrapati Bhavan, Parliament House (Sansad Bhavan), Supreme Court
Status: Union Territory with Legislative Assembly

title: Capital of Jammu and Kashmir — Srinagar (Summer) / Jammu (Winter)
answer: Srinagar is the summer capital and Jammu is the winter capital of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
highlights: Summer Capital: Srinagar (Dal Lake, Mughal Gardens)

title: Capital of Ladakh — Leh (Summer) / Kargil (Winter)
answer: Leh is the summer capital and Kargil is the winter capital of the Union Territory of Ladakh, India's high-altitude cold desert region.
highlights: Status: Union Territory created on 31 October 2019
Geography: High altitude Himalayan cold desert

title: Capital of Andaman and Nicobar Islands — Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair)
answer: Sri Vijaya Puram (formerly Port Blair) is the capital city of the Union Territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
highlights: Location: South Andaman Island, Bay of Bengal

title: Capital of Chandigarh — Chandigarh
answer: Chandigarh is a Union Territory that serves as its own capital as well as the joint capital for Punjab and Haryana.

keywords: capital of dadra and nagar haveli and daman and diu
title: Capital of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu — Daman
answer: Daman is the capital of the merged Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

title: Capital of Lakshadweep — Kavaratti
answer: Kavaratti is the capital of the Union Territory of Lakshadweep, an archipelago in the Arabian Sea.
highlights: Geography: 36 coral atolls and islands in the Arabian Sea
Smallest UT: Land area of only 32 km²

title: Capital of Puducherry — Pondicherry (Puducherry)
answer: Puducherry (Pondicherry) is the capital of the Union Territory of Puducherry, known for its French colonial heritage and Auroville.
highlights: Former Rule: French India colony until 1954

title: Capital of France — Paris
answer: Paris is the capital and largest city of France, situated along the Seine River.
highlights: Landmarks: Eiffel Tower, Louvre, Notre-Dame, Arc de Triomphe

title: Capital of Japan — Tokyo
answer: Tokyo is the capital of Japan and the world's most populous metropolitan area.

title: Capital of the United States — Washington, D.C.
answer: Washington, D.C. (District of Columbia) is the federal capital of the United States of America.
highlights: Seat of Government: White House, Capitol Hill, Supreme Court

title: Capital of the United Kingdom — London
answer: London is the capital and largest city of England and the United Kingdom, standing on the River Thames.
highlights: Landmarks: Big Ben, Tower of London, Buckingham Palace, British Museum

title: Capital of Australia — Canberra
answer: Canberra is the capital city of Australia, situated within the Australian Capital Territory (ACT).
highlights: Chosen In: 1908 as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne

title: Capital of Germany — Berlin
answer: Berlin is the capital and largest city of Germany by both area and population.
highlights: Landmarks: Brandenburg Gate, Reichstag Building, Berlin Wall Memorial

title: Capital of Canada — Ottawa
answer: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, located in the province of Ontario on the south bank of the Ottawa River.

title: Capital of Russia — Moscow
answer: Moscow is the capital and largest city of the Russian Federation, situated along the Moskva River.
highlights: Country: Russia (largest country in world by area)
Landmarks: Red Square, Kremlin, Saint Basil's Cathedral

title: Capital of China — Beijing
answer: Beijing (Peking) is the capital city of the People's Republic of China, with over 3,000 years of rich history.
highlights: Landmarks: Forbidden City, Tiananmen Square, Great Wall of China

title: Capital of Italy — Rome
answer: Rome is the capital city of Italy, known as the 'Eternal City' and home to the Vatican City enclave.
highlights: Landmarks: Colosseum, Roman Forum, Trevi Fountain, Pantheon

title: Capital of Brazil — Brasília
answer: Brasília is the federal capital of Brazil, inaugurated in 1960 as a planned city designed by Oscar Niemeyer and Lúcio Costa.
highlights: Design: Planned city shaped like an airplane

title: Capital of Saudi Arabia — Riyadh
answer: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

title: Capital of the United Arab Emirates — Abu Dhabi
answer: Abu Dhabi is the capital and second-most populous city of the United Arab Emirates (after Dubai).
highlights: Landmarks: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Louvre Abu Dhabi

title: Capital of Pakistan — Islamabad
answer: Islamabad is the federal capital city of Pakistan, located in the Islamabad Capital Territory in the foothills of the Margalla Hills.
highlights: Built In: 1960s to replace Karachi as capital

title: Capital of Bangladesh — Dhaka
answer: Dhaka is the capital and largest megacity of Bangladesh, situated along the Buriganga River.
highlights: Nickname: City of Mosques / Rickshaw Capital of the World

title: Capital of Nepal — Kathmandu
answer: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal, set in the Kathmandu Valley in the Himalayas.
highlights: Landmarks: Pashupatinath Temple, Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), Boudhanath

title: Capital of Sri Lanka — Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte / Colombo
answer: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the legislative capital and Colombo is the executive, judicial, and commercial capital of Sri Lanka.

title: Capital of Spain — Madrid
answer: Madrid is the capital and largest city of Spain, located in the central part of the Iberian Peninsula on the Manzanares River.
highlights: Landmarks: Royal Palace of Madrid, Prado Museum

title: Capital of South Korea — Seoul
answer: Seoul is the capital and largest metropolis of South Korea, located on the Han River.
highlights: Landmarks: Gyeongbokgung Palace, N Seoul Tower, Lotte World Tower

title: Capitals of South Africa — Pretoria / Cape Town / Bloemfontein
answer: South Africa has three official capital cities: Pretoria (Executive / Administrative), Cape Town (Legislative), and Bloemfontein (Judicial).

title: Capital of Egypt — Cairo
answer: Cairo is the capital and largest city of Egypt and the Arab world, situated near the Nile River Delta.
highlights: Landmarks: Giza Pyramids, Great Sphinx, Grand Egyptian Museum

title: Capital of Mexico — Mexico City
answer: Mexico City is the capital and largest city of Mexico, built on the historic ruins of Tenochtitlan in the Valley of Mexico.

title: Capital of Argentina — Buenos Aires
answer: Buenos Aires is the capital and largest city of Argentina, located on the western shore of the Río de la Plata estuary.
highlights: Landmarks: Casa Rosada, Plaza de Mayo, Teatro Colón, Obelisco

title: Capital of Indonesia — Jakarta (transitioning to Nusantara)
answer: Jakarta is the current capital and largest city of Indonesia, with Nusantara in East Kalimantan designated as the future planned administrative capital.

title: Capital of Turkey (Türkiye) — Ankara
answer: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey (Türkiye), situated in the central Anatolia region, while Istanbul is its largest city.

title: De Facto Capital of Switzerland — Bern
answer: Bern is the de facto capital (Federal City) and seat of government of Switzerland.
highlights: Federal City / De Facto Capital: Bern

title: Capital of the Netherlands — Amsterdam (The Hague seat of govt)
answer: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands, while The Hague is the seat of its government, parliament, and Supreme Court.
highlights: Seat of Government & International Courts: The Hague
